patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every route in scope is a write path; there is no read decision to omit
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the upload path parses no identity or role claim; the upload id is sanitized and is not an authorization input
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: permission evaluation is closed by default (a role without the action is denied and the anonymous role denies); the upload path carries no optional authority value

traps.shape: Authorization is absent at the staging write: the create route appends the first part of an upload to the upload staging area before the file the completed upload would create is authorized.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the commit-time rule already refuses the finished file and the uploader comment says the chunk is validated again by createFile, so the early write reads as an ordering detail

traps.shape: The declared file type exists only as the constructor-supplied argument for field uploads, while the request body is the obvious source for a decision; a body-only decision silently judges the default type.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the field mixin passes the type only as an Api::upload argument, and the existing pinned test pins the argument over the body as the winning value

traps.shape: The decision must be made on a File built from the target parent and the declared type, because the type's own options block takes priority over the role defaults; a role-only decision mis-decides both ways.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: ModelPermissions consults the blueprint options before the role permissions, so the role category alone is not the authorization subject

traps.shape: The replace route is the same uploader with a different action and target: the decision is file replace on the target file, not file create on the parent.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the replace route calls the same upload helper as the create route, and the commit-time replace rule makes the early write look harmless

traps.shape: The avatar route targets a user account, so the decision is account update, and updating one's own account is a different permission category from updating another account.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the route already picks createAvatar or replaceAvatar from the current state and the user rule checks update at commit time, so the early write reads as covered

traps.shape: Nothing pins the declared file type and total length of a multi-request upload, so a later request can substitute a more permissive type and a different total before the final create reads its own declaration.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: requests are stateless and each request validates itself, and createFile re-validates the finished file against the completing request's own declaration

traps.shape: Chunk-time name validation judges the id-prefixed temporary name instead of the name that will be stored, so a banned final name (a server-config or hidden file) passes into the staging area.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the pinned commit builds the validation subject from the temporary path, and the published fix does not touch that line

a.summary: API upload pre-flight before staging, plus a pinned declared file type and total length for multi-request uploads
